name: Cascade Intuition
classification: Cybernetic Predictive Enhancement / Neural Pattern Amplification
mechanism: Cascade Intuition is the product of a specific cortical implant cluster — three nodes placed in the parietal-temporal junction, the anterior cingulate cortex, and the prefrontal decision architecture — that collectively amplify the brain's existing pattern-recognition circuitry. The human brain already performs unconscious probabilistic modeling from environmental inputs: micro-expressions, gait analysis, environmental change detection, acoustic pattern matching. The Cascade implant does not add new capability. It removes the cognitive suppression that prevents this processing from reaching conscious awareness. The result is that the subject begins receiving, as conscious experience, the output of prediction systems that previously operated without generating reportable thought. They do not see the future. They see, with uncomfortable clarity, the extremely high-probability near-term present.
abilities: Subjects with functioning Cascade implants report a consistent experience of knowing things slightly before they happen — not prophecy, not precognition in any supernatural sense, but the unnerving experience of having already processed an outcome that has not yet occurred. In practical terms: knowing who is about to come through a door from micro-acoustic cues below normal conscious hearing threshold. Reading the intent of a person across a room from posture and micro-expression processing before the person has acted on that intent. Identifying structural weak points in a physical environment from the way sound and vibration propagate through it. Making correct probability assessments under time pressure without conscious calculation. In the right operational context, the Cascade is close to the most useful thing money can buy.
side_effects: The suppression systems the Cascade removes were doing something useful. The human brain does not report most of its pattern-recognition output to consciousness because consciousness cannot coherently process the volume of probabilistic information the brain generates. With the suppression removed, the subject begins receiving signal noise alongside signal — false positives from the pattern-recognition system, probabilistic outputs that are high-confidence but wrong, misread inputs that the system processes with the same confidence as correct reads. This presents as a specific and initially difficult-to-identify cognitive symptom: a persistent low-grade conviction that something is about to happen, frequently wrong, always emotionally present. The clinical term for this in subjects with degraded implant calibration is 'perpetual imminence' — the continuous experience of being on the verge of something without the something materializing. Advanced cases present with decision paralysis, because the subject cannot distinguish signal from noise in the flood of predictions. Terminal cases: the implant's amplification gradually cannot be turned off, and the subject loses the ability to process the present because they are continuously processing the near-future that never quite arrives.
acquisition_method: Commercial availability through licensed neural modification clinics, though the quality of implant and calibration varies enormously by provider. The full three-node Cascade as originally developed by Helix Biosystems (before the program was reclassified) requires surgical installation by a qualified neurotechnician and a calibration period of four to six weeks during which the subject adjusts to the new signal volume. The black market version — a single-node approximation that targets only the anterior cingulate — produces a cruder version of the effect with significantly higher noise-to-signal ratio and elevated risk of perpetual imminence onset. Price range: Φ 40,000–180,000 depending on provider and implant quality.
detection_risk: Moderate. The implants are radio-frequency detectable by standard security screening. The behavioral effects of the Cascade — the slightly-too-early responses, the anomalous situational awareness — are not immediately distinguishable from skilled training to most observers, but are recognizable to other Cascade subjects and to intelligence analysts trained in psionic detection screening. Several corponations have deployed Cascade-detection protocols in high-security interview and interrogation contexts.
corporate_interest: The original development program was Helix Biosystems, which reclassified the project after the second generation of subjects showed the perpetual imminence degradation pathway. The current commercial market is dominated by two clinics operating under different licensing arrangements with the original patent holders. At least three corponations — Dreadnaught Incorporated, Axiom Meridian's intelligence division, and a smaller entity believed to be a subsidiary of Vantage Collective — have Cascade-equipped operative programs. The research frontier is second-generation implants designed to address the noise-to-signal problem without sacrificing sensitivity.
known_practitioners: Unconfirmed: several documented DPS field commanders display behavioral signatures consistent with Cascade installation
At least twelve known independent contractors in the GLMZ runner community are confirmed or suspected Cascade subjects
story_hooks: A runner's Cascade implant has started degrading — perpetual imminence is setting in, and the noise is getting worse. The job they've been hired for requires exactly the capability the Cascade provides at its best. The question is whether they can complete it before they can no longer tell what they're actually predicting versus what the noise is generating.

A new version of the Cascade is on the market — a third-generation implant that claims to have solved the noise problem. A corponation is paying well for field testers willing to have the experimental implant installed. The catch is the consent form's section on known risks, which is three pages long and includes a phrase that reads 'temporal integration events of unclear etiology.'

Someone with a Cascade is being very careful not to use it during a specific job. They've been hired specifically for the predictive capability and they are deliberately not deploying it. The client has noticed. The runner needs to understand why before deciding whether to ask.
